title: What are FAANG stocks?
summary: FAANG is an acronym for five leading technology companies: Facebook (now Meta), Amazon, Apple, Netflix, and Google (now Alphabet). These companies are known for their consistent growth, innovation, and significant impact on the American stock market, particularly the NASDAQ 100 and S&P 500 indices. While they have shown strong performance and market capitalization, there's an ongoing debate among investors about their valuation.

title: Up in the Cloud!
summary: This article by Uma Iyer discusses the evolving concept of cloud computing, moving beyond its abstract perception to its tangible impact on technology and data management. It explores the differences between cloud storage and cloud computing, highlights real-world applications and the benefits of scalability and ease of use, and addresses the critical issue of trust and security in cloud technologies through various models and programs like CSA STAR. The article concludes by looking at emerging trends like edge computing, indicating a bright future for cloud technology.

title: Zscaler and AWS to help customers accelerate their secured transition to the cloud
summary: Zscaler has extended its relationship with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to help customers securely transition to the cloud using a Zero Trust approach. The collaboration introduces new solutions, including a Cloud-Native Application Protection Platform (CNAPP) built on AWS, extended Zero Trust security for cloud workloads, and Zero Trust for Private 5G connections with AWS Wavelength. These innovations aim to simplify cloud security operations, mitigate workload risks, and advance security architecture for enterprises.

title: How Much Worse Can It Get for Growth Stocks?
summary: The second quarter of 2022 saw growth stocks suffer their largest losses since the 2008 financial crisis, with the Morningstar US Growth Index dropping 25.3%. Value stocks significantly outperformed growth, marking the widest margin since the dot-com bubble collapse, as rising interest rates and inflation dampened the appeal of growth companies' future earnings. While many growth stocks are now at their cheapest valuations in years, experts suggest value stocks may continue to outperform in the short term despite growth's long-term lead.

title: Walt Disney Co. Creates ‘Disney Storytellers Fund’ At Howard University To Spark Opportunities
summary: The Walt Disney Company has established the "Disney Storytellers Fund" at Howard University. This initiative aims to provide opportunities for underrepresented students to pursue careers in media and entertainment, offering stipends, mentorship, and internships across various creative fields. The fund will also support a new collaborative creative space within Howard's Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts and Cathy Hughes School of Communication.

title: 5 Indian Americans among America’s Richest Self-Made Women
summary: Five Indian American women, including Jayshree Ullal, Neerja Sethi, Neha Narkhede, Indra Nooyi, and Reshma Shetty, have been named among America's Richest Self-Made Women by Forbes in 2022. These women have accumulated significant wealth across various industries such as technology, consulting, and biotechnology. The article highlights their career paths, companies, and net worth, showcasing their success and contributions to the American economy.

title: When Pentest Tools Go Brutal: Red-Teaming Tool Being Abused by Malicious Actors
summary: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 has identified that Brute Ratel C4 (BRc4), a red-teaming and adversarial attack simulation tool designed to evade EDR and AV detection, is being actively abused by malicious actors, including techniques consistent with APT29. The tool's effectiveness was highlighted by a sample that received benign verdicts from all 56 VirusTotal vendors despite containing a malicious payload. The report details the technical analysis of how BRc4 is deployed, including DLL search order hijacking and process injection, and provides indicators of compromise to help organizations detect and protect against this evolving threat.

title: Top 15 Affirm Competitors and Alternatives
summary: This article identifies and details the top 15 competitors and alternatives to Affirm, a leading buy now, pay later (BNPL) service provider. It highlights various companies like Sezzle, PayPal, Klarna, Afterpay, and Zip, outlining their services, financial performance, and unique features. The piece also discusses alternatives that cater to specific needs, such as travel payments (Uplift) or those for consumers with poor credit (Perpay).

title: 'A certification that you've made it': How United Natural Foods Inc became the DTC CPG gatekeeper
summary: United Natural Foods, Inc. (UNFI) has established itself as the leading wholesale distributor for health and specialty foods in North America, becoming a crucial gateway for DTC brands aiming for national retail presence. Despite challenges like antiquated processes and margin compromises, working with UNFI is often a necessary "certification" for CPG startups seeking to expand beyond e-commerce into major grocery chains like Whole Foods. The article highlights UNFI's significant influence and role in bridging digitally-native brands with traditional physical retail, as demonstrated by brand experiences and financial figures, including $27.27 billion in revenue in 2021.

title: Springfield trucking company settles lawsuit with Amazon over use of word 'Prime'
summary: Springfield-based trucking company Prime Inc. has settled a lawsuit with Amazon regarding Amazon's use of the word "Prime" on its shipping vehicles. Prime Inc. had sued Amazon in 2019, claiming the retailer's use of "Prime" caused confusion and potential "irreparable injury" to its business, which has used the name on its semi-trailers since at least 1980. The terms of the confidential settlement were not disclosed, and representatives from both companies declined to comment on whether Amazon would cease using "Prime" on its vehicles.

title: Amazon Celebrates Prime Members With New, Exclusive Offers and Experiences
summary: Amazon announced new exclusive offers and experiences for Prime members, ahead of Prime Day on July 12-13. These include a free one-year Grubhub+ membership, an exclusive 60-second sneak peek of "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" for 48 hours, and special deals on electronics and fan gear for the upcoming Thursday Night Football on Prime Video. The company emphasizes the enhanced value and expanded benefits now available to its Prime members.

title: Qualys Launches VMDR 2.0 with TruRisk™ Scores and Automated Remediation Workflows
summary: Qualys (NASDAQ: QLYS) has launched VMDR 2.0 with TruRisk™ scores and automated remediation workflows, aiming to provide organizations with clearer insights into their risk posture. This new cloud-based solution helps security and IT teams prioritize and respond to critical threats more efficiently by integrating risk-based vulnerability management, correlating vulnerabilities with business criticality, and automating remediation processes through drag-and-drop workflows. Beta customers reportedly reduced critical vulnerabilities by 28% and risk by an average of 23%.

title: Shopee opens five new distribution centers in Brazil - report
summary: Shopee, the Singaporean shopping app owned by Sea Ltd (SE.N), has opened five new distribution centers in Brazil to enhance shipping and reduce delivery times. The new centers are located in Sao Joao do Meriti, Campinas, Ribeirao Preto, Contagem, and Santana do Parnaiba, supporting the high volume of low-unit-price goods sold on the platform. This expansion comes after a period of strong growth for Shopee in Brazil, despite Sea's broader challenges with rising costs and market exits in other regions.

title: Deezer stock listing: Why did the Spotify rival crash on its first day of trading?
summary: Deezer's stock crashed on its first day of trading in the French markets, despite initial high hopes for its public offering through a SPAC. The company's valuation significantly dropped from an anticipated €1.1 billion to €677 million. This poor performance is attributed to the intense competition from larger tech giants like Apple and Amazon, which have diverse revenue streams, and a general cooling of investor interest in tech stocks amidst rising inflation and recession fears in 2022.

title: Amazon and Microsoft deny using Flickr pics for facial recognition, as suits test limits of privacy law
summary: Amazon and Microsoft are facing lawsuits alleging they violated the Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act by using Flickr photos for facial recognition development without consent. Both companies deny using the IBM "Diversity in Faces" database for their AI algorithms after initial downloads. The cases highlight broader issues concerning the lack of a national privacy law, the trade-offs between privacy and AI accuracy, and jurisdictional complexities in the cloud era.

title: TV Personality, Entrepreneur and QVC Star Kim Gravel Signs Book Deal with Thomas Nelson; Inspirational Memoir to come April 2023
summary: Kim Gravel, a well-known TV personality, entrepreneur, and QVC star, has signed a book deal with Thomas Nelson for her first inspirational memoir, "Collecting Confidence: Start Where You Are to Become the Person You Were Meant to Be." The book is scheduled for release in April 2023 and aims to empower women to embrace their inner beauty and confidence. Gravel, known for her successful brands Belle by Kim Gravel and Belle Beauty on QVC, seeks to share her life experiences to inspire readers to overcome challenges and recognize their innate greatness.

title: Why Adobe Stock Is Down 35% So Far in 2022
summary: Adobe's stock has dropped 35% in the first half of 2022 due to a slowing growth pace, despite strong sales and cash flow. Investors are concerned about a "growth hangover" as work patterns normalize post-pandemic, leading to a conservative outlook from management for the latter half of the year. While the company still expects strong sales for 2022, the short-term market focus on decelerating demand is pressuring the stock.

title: Kirkland’s launches in-home delivery service
summary: Kirkland's Inc. is launching a new in-home delivery service, partnering with Ryder System Inc. to provide last-mile delivery, light assembly, and packaging disposal for large home decor and furniture products. This nationwide program, initially test-launched in over 25 markets in June 2022, is expected to cover the lower 48 U.S. states by the end of July 2022. The move aims to enhance customer experience, expand the customer base, and make Kirkland's offerings more competitive, following a trend among other retailers offering assembly services.

title: Uber expanding business to Israel
summary: Uber is launching its ride-hailing app in Israel, five years after a previous attempt failed, by partnering with a network of licensed taxi drivers. The service will be available in Jerusalem and Tel Aviv, competing with existing local services. This expansion is part of Uber's global strategy to integrate taxis into its app, following similar partnerships in several other countries.

title: FMET Makes It Simple to Take Long View of Metaverse
summary: The Fidelity Metaverse ETF (FMET) offers investors a way to engage with the growing metaverse theme, which is projected to be worth over $800 million by 2028. Despite a retrenchment in growth stocks, the long-term outlook for the metaverse remains compelling, especially with established companies like Meta Platforms, Alphabet, Apple, and Nvidia investing heavily in its development. FMET provides a diversified basket approach to this theme, including exposure to gaming and numerous mega-cap growth companies, with an affordable annual fee.

title: Amazon Fresh store now open steps from HQ2
summary: Amazon has opened a new Amazon Fresh grocery store in Crystal City, just steps from its HQ2. This location marks the third Amazon Fresh store to open in the last month. The store was reported on by Hannah Denham of the Washington Business Journal.

title: QQ Music introduces Dolby Atmos support
summary: QQ Music, a leading Chinese music streaming service, has introduced Dolby Atmos support through a strategic partnership between Tencent Music Entertainment and Dolby. This integration brings spatial audio to the platform, making QQ Music the first domestic streaming service in China to offer Dolby Atmos, initially available to SVIP subscribers on compatible Android devices and featuring a growing catalog of international and Chinese artists. The collaboration aims to enhance the music listening experience for users in China.

title: Global Industrial Continues Sales Structure Diversification
summary: Global Industrial is diversifying its sales structure, moving from a historically inside sales-based model to incorporating a direct sales channel and emphasizing vertical alignment. CSO Claudia Hughes discusses the company's hybrid digital-inside-outside sales model, its focus on strategic account managers, new business development, and the impact of remote work on sales team engagement and customer interaction while maintaining differentiation against competitors.

title: Canadian Solar sells two Australian solar farms to US interests
summary: Canadian Solar has sold its 150 MW Suntop Solar Farm and 110 MW Gunnedah Solar Farm in New South Wales, Australia, to CalEnergy Resources, a subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway Energy. The deal also includes a multi-year development services agreement for Canadian Solar to build out CalEnergy's renewable energy pipeline in Australia. These solar farms are backed by long-term offtake agreements with Amazon and are expected to generate over 700,000 MWh annually, avoiding significant CO2 emissions.

title: The Weekly Closeout: Ulta, The Allure Store partner and UK antitrust watchdog takes on Amazon
summary: This weekly retail wrap-up covers Ulta Beauty's pop-up shop at The Allure Store in NYC, focusing on highlighting newer brands and experiential programming. It also details Deckers' hiring of former Nike chief merchant Anne Spangenberg to lead its fashion and lifestyle brands. Additionally, the article reports on the UK's Competition and Markets Authority launching an antitrust probe into Amazon's marketplace practices, following similar investigations in the EU, and touches on other retail news like E.l.f.'s gaming-inspired makeup and Aldi's anti-theft measures.

title: What the Shopify stock split means for investors
summary: This article discusses the implications of Shopify Inc.'s 10-to-1 stock split on June 29, 2022, following a significant drop in its share price. It explores the strategic benefits of such a split, including making shares more attractive to retail investors, improving liquidity, and potentially boosting the share price. The article also examines the initial impact on Shopify's stock performance and trading activity.

title: Florida man charged with selling fake Cisco equipment in $1 billion scheme
summary: A Florida man, Onur Aksoy, has been charged with importing and reselling counterfeit Cisco networking equipment worth over $1 billion if authentic. Aksoy allegedly operated a scheme from 2013 to 2022, netting $100 million in revenue by selling fake devices through Amazon.com, eBay, and other platforms after acquiring them from suppliers in China and Hong Kong. Cisco Systems Inc. sent multiple cease-and-desist letters, and both Amazon and eBay blocked numerous storefronts related to the counterfeiting.

title: The next evolution of the Dash Cart: New features and expansion to first Whole Foods Market Store
summary: Amazon has released an upgraded version of its Dash Cart, a smart shopping cart designed to make grocery trips quicker by allowing customers to skip checkout lines. The new Dash Cart offers increased capacity, weather resistance, improved product recognition, and extended battery life, based on customer feedback and technological advancements. This enhanced version will be introduced at a Whole Foods Market store in Westford, Massachusetts, and subsequently rolled out to more Whole Foods Market and Amazon Fresh locations.

title: Bath & Body Works changes return policy
summary: Bath & Body Works is updating its return policy, effective September 14, to limit non-receipted returns or exchanges to $250 within a 90-day period at select U.S. stores. The company will use an electronic system for tracking these returns, requiring customers to show a government-issued ID. While maintaining a 100% satisfaction guarantee, the updated policy will no longer accept products showing excessive wear and tear.

title: Behind the scenes: Same-day Amazon shipping facility in Utah preps for Prime Day 2022
summary: Amazon's same-day fulfillment center in Salt Lake City, Utah, is gearing up for Prime Day 2022, anticipating a significant spike in demand despite rising inflation. The 150,000-square-foot facility, which delivers within an hour's radius, stores essential household goods and handles 20,000 to 25,000 packages daily, a number expected to surge during the two-day sales event. The center utilizes 2,500 robotic drives to efficiently process orders, ensuring quick delivery by flex drivers using their own vehicles.

title: HPE exec: GreenLake is to HPE as AWS is to Amazon
summary: Omer Asad, VP and GM at HPE, explains that GreenLake is central to HPE's transformation into a platform company, akin to how AWS functions for Amazon or Azure for Microsoft. GreenLake offers customers a cloud-like consumption experience for infrastructure, moving away from traditional hardware sales to a service-based model. This shift addresses customer desires for simplified infrastructure consumption and outcome-based solutions rather than focusing on raw hardware specifications.

title: NetApp Ontap to be sole vSAN storage alternative in the cloud
summary: NetApp's Ontap-based cloud storage services will become the exclusive vSAN storage alternative officially supported by VMware's vSphere instances in the cloud. This partnership allows enterprise customers to extend VMware data stores in AWS, Azure, and Google clouds using Ontap as an external NFS data store, offering a more cost-effective solution than traditional vSAN. The move aims to provide a familiar and integrated storage experience for VMware customers migrating to the cloud.

title: EXCLUSIVE BC Partners explores $4 bln sale of IT firm Presidio -sources
summary: Private equity firm BC Partners Ltd is reportedly exploring the sale of Presidio Inc., a U.S. information technology provider, for over $4 billion, including debt. Presidio, which generated $3.1 billion in revenue in 2021, specializes in secured cloud-based technology for a wide range of organizations and has benefited from increased demand for IT services during the COVID-19 pandemic. This potential sale follows a history of private equity ownership, with BC Partners having taken the company private in 2019 for $2.1 billion.

title: Check Point Software Technologies announces the integration of CloudGuard Network Security with AWS Cloud WAN Service
summary: Check Point Software Technologies has announced the integration of its CloudGuard Network Security with the new AWS Cloud WAN service. This integration aims to simplify the deployment of complex and resilient cloud architectures for organizations transitioning to the cloud, providing industry-leading security for network traffic and consistent security policies across AWS and hybrid-cloud deployments. CloudGuard Network Security, a cloud-native security gateway, enhances AWS Cloud WAN by offering advanced threat prevention, visibility, and posture management alongside existing AWS services.

title: Cisco SD-WAN with AWS Cloud WAN for an on-demand global cloud network
summary: Cisco and AWS are collaborating to integrate Cisco SD-WAN with AWS Cloud WAN, aiming to simplify and accelerate cloud journeys for their joint customers. This integration allows organizations to connect multi-region and cloud-to-on-premises workloads with enhanced automation, unified management, and secure cloud networking. The solution will reduce deployment times, lower TCO, and provide a single portal experience for secure connectivity across AWS cloud regions.

title: AWS Selected as Delta’s Preferred Cloud Provider
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has been selected as Delta Air Lines' preferred cloud provider in a multi-year agreement. This partnership aims to accelerate Delta's digital business transformation by using AWS's cloud technologies to enhance customer experience, streamline processes, and provide cloud training to its employees globally. The collaboration will also modernize Delta's core technology platforms, including its customer engagement center operations using Amazon Connect, and extends to Amazon being Delta's most preferred carrier for business travel.

title: Western Digital Releases First Officially Licensed M.2 SSD for the Sony PlayStation 5
summary: Western Digital and Sony Interactive Entertainment have partnered to release the industry's first official PlayStation-licensed M.2 SSD for the PlayStation 5. The WD_BLACK SN850 NVMe SSD for PS5 Consoles allows gamers to expand their console's storage with a drive optimized and tested for intensive PS5 gameplay, offering speeds up to 7000 MB/s. It is available for $169.99 (1 TB) and $279.99 (2 TB) at Best Buy and Western Digital's online store, with wider availability coming in mid-August 2022.

title: What Does Google’s Stock Split Mean for Investors?
summary: Google's parent company, Alphabet, is undergoing a 20-for-1 stock split, which will adjust Morningstar's fair value estimate per share to $180, though its competitive advantage and 4-star "undervalued" rating remain unchanged. Analyst Ali Mogharabi identifies YouTube monetization, Maps monetization, and the cloud business as key growth drivers, with strong confidence in Google's continued dominance in the online search market. The article also notes other companies like Amazon, Shopify, and Tesla undertaking similar stock splits.

title: Goldman hires Google exec to co-head applied innovation unit - memo
summary: Goldman Sachs has appointed Jared Cohen, founder of Google's Jigsaw technology incubator, to co-head its new applied innovation unit. This move signifies Goldman's increased investment in technology and its push to leverage internal talent and external relationships for business growth and new ventures. Cohen will share leadership with George Lee, who will transition to the unit after October 1st, at which point Marco Argenti will become the sole chief information officer.

title: Amazon, Moov to have offices ready at new Tempe high-rise early next year
summary: Amazon and Moov are set to occupy offices at the new 100 Mill high-rise in Tempe starting early next year. Developed by Hines and Cousins Properties, the building is already 92% leased, with Amazon taking five floors. This development highlights ongoing growth in the Tempe office market.

title: Dollar Store Workers Organizing for Justice
summary: Dollar store workers are organizing nationwide to combat poor working conditions, low pay, and safety concerns prevalent in the sector. Despite aggressive anti-union tactics from companies like Dollar General, employees are increasingly seeking union representation, forming groups like Dollar Store Workers United Association. They aim to improve wages, staffing levels, and store safety, drawing inspiration from other successful retail unionization campaigns.

title: Stock-Split Watch: Is Adobe Next?
summary: Adobe could be the next high-profile company to announce a stock split, following a trend set by others like Alphabet and Amazon in 2022. While stock splits don't alter a company's fundamental valuation, they can make shares more accessible to retail investors and help companies attract/retain talent. Adobe has a history of 2-for-1 splits, with its last one occurring 17 years ago, and its strong financial performance in Q2 2022 suggests a healthy business that could support such a move.

title: ETF 360: Q&A With Simeon Hyman
summary: This "ETF 360" episode features Todd Rosenbluth and Simeon Hyman discussing the ProShares Online Retail ETF (ONLN), highlighting the continued growth of e-commerce despite some pandemic-driven fluctuations. Hyman explains that online retail, including major global players like Amazon and Alibaba, has significant growth potential and that the ONLN ETF—with its global, market-cap-weighted portfolio—offers investors access to this sector at a substantial discount compared to the broader consumer discretionary sector. The ETF can serve as a thematic satellite or a consumer discretionary representative in portfolios.

title: How to Buy Google Stock After the Split: GOOG vs. GOOGL
summary: Alphabet (Google's parent company) completed a 20-for-one stock split on July 15, 2022, making its shares more accessible to retail investors by lowering the per-share price. The article explains that Alphabet trades under two ticker symbols, GOOG (Class C, non-voting) and GOOGL (Class A, voting rights), both of which were affected by the split. Existing shareholders did not need to take any action as their accounts were automatically updated to reflect the new share quantity and price.

title: Prime Day 2022 was the biggest Prime Day event ever
summary: Prime Day 2022 proved to be the largest Prime Day event in Amazon's history, with members purchasing over 300 million items worldwide and saving more than $1.7 billion. This year also marked the biggest Prime Day for Amazon's small and medium-sized selling partners, whose sales growth outpaced Amazon's retail business. Customers spent over $3 billion on small business items, highlighting a significant focus on supporting these businesses during the event.

title: ‘Netflix Thinks Exactly Like an Old Movie Studio’
summary: In response to declining subscriber numbers and a volatile stock price, Netflix is shifting its strategy from filling niche content gaps to focusing on expensive, large-scale, and risky blockbusters with A-list stars. This pivot aims to compete directly with traditional Hollywood studios by creating new, wide-reaching franchises, despite lacking the same intellectual property. The company hopes these "event" films will re-engage audiences and solidify Netflix's position in the streaming landscape.

title: Online sales nationwide spike during Amazon Prime Day event
summary: Online spending in the U.S. during the 48-hour Amazon Prime Day event reached almost $12 billion, as other retailers also leveraged the period. Amazon sold over 300 million items during its Prime Day, with these sales to be reported in its fiscal third-quarter earnings. The article also touches on Amazon's expanding e-commerce lead and related sales trends.

title: BMW: New Subscription Fees for Heated Seats Won’t Impact U.S.
summary: BMW has announced that new subscription fees for heated seats will not apply to its vehicles sold in the U.S. In the U.S., subscription services are limited to BMW Drive Recorder and remote start, offered through BMW's ConnectedDrive. This decision follows previous customer backlash against a subscription model for Apple CarPlay and highlights a broader reluctance among U.S. car shoppers to pay for subscription-based features.

title: Medtronic expands Health Equity Assistance Program for colon cancer screening with support from Amazon Web Services; Completes first installation of donated GI Genius™ intelligent endoscopy modules
summary: Medtronic announced the expansion of its Health Equity Assistance Program for colon cancer screening, supported by Amazon Web Services, increasing the number of donated GI Genius™ intelligent endoscopy modules from 50 to 133 across 62 facilities. Grady Memorial Hospital in Atlanta received the first installation of these modules, which use AI to detect colorectal polyps, addressing disparities in communities with low screening rates. This initiative aims to improve early detection and outcomes for colon cancer, particularly among vulnerable populations that disproportionately experience higher rates of the disease.

title: Daily deals July 17: $130 Apple TV 4K, $700 off 55-inch LG OLED Smart TV, $27 Netgear router, more
summary: This article lists the best daily deals for July 17, including significant discounts on an Apple TV 4K, a 55-inch LG OLED Smart TV, and a Netgear router. It compiles offers from various online stores like Amazon and Walmart, advising readers to act quickly as deals can be short-lived. The piece also mentions ongoing deals from the previous day.

title: What Does GameStop’s Stock Split Mean for Investors?
summary: GameStop (GME) is undergoing a 4-for-1 stock split, its first in 15 years, which will increase the number of shares and decrease the price per share without affecting market capitalization. Morningstar gives GME a 3-star quantitative rating, indicating it is fairly valued, but with extreme uncertainty due to high volatility. This split follows similar actions by other tech and consumer companies like Amazon, Shopify, and Alphabet.

title: Amazon’s Prime Video streamlines its user interface with a new look
summary: Amazon's Prime Video is updating its user interface and home screen, introducing new features like a "Top 10 most popular shows" list. The redesign will initially roll out to TV and Android app users in mid-August, with web and iOS users receiving the update later this year. This overhaul aims to improve the user experience ahead of major fall releases.

title: The Critiques Against the American Innovation and Choice Online Act Miss the Mark
summary: Yelp's General Counsel, Aaron Schur, argues that criticisms against the American Innovation and Choice Online Act (AICOA) are unfounded and focus on highly unlikely hypothetical abuses. He contends that concerns about the bill hindering content moderation are misguided, as existing antitrust laws and judicial precedent would prevent such misapplications. Schur asserts that the proposed edits to AICOA are unnecessary, politically unfeasible, and would weaken antitrust enforcement, urging legislators to pass the bill as is to combat real anticompetitive harms.

title: LinkedIn Still Number One Brand to be Faked in Phishing Attempts while Microsoft Surges up the Rankings to Number Two Spot in Q2 Report
summary: Check Point Research's Q2 Brand Phishing Report reveals that LinkedIn remains the most imitated brand in phishing attempts, accounting for 45% of all such attacks. Microsoft has significantly risen to the second spot with 13%, surpassing DHL, while new brands like Adidas, Adobe, and HSBC have entered the top 10. The report highlights the dangers of these scams, with examples provided for LinkedIn, DHL, Outlook, and Amazon phishing attempts.

title: STACKTV’S SUITE OF HIT SHOWS AND MOVIES NOW AVAILABLE ON FUBOTV
summary: Corus Entertainment's STACKTV is expanding its distribution by partnering with FuboTV, making its premium content available to FuboTV's Canadian subscribers. This collaboration integrates STACKTV's hit shows and news programs from 13 Canadian networks into FuboTV's new "Premium" subscription package, enhancing FuboTV's offerings beyond its sports-first content. The move aims to provide more Canadians with broader access to diverse entertainment and news, reinforcing STACKTV's market presence.

title: This is how much more an S&P 500 CEO earned than the typical worker last year
summary: A new report from the AFL-CIO reveals that S&P 500 CEOs earned an average of $18.3 million in total compensation in 2021, which is 324 times more than their median-paid workers. This compensation marked a significant increase that outpaced inflation, further widening the gap between executive and worker pay. The report highlights this disparity at major companies like Amazon, Expedia Group, McDonald’s, and The TJX Companies.

title: A.I.-powered robotic lawnmowers help you reclaim your summer days
summary: Robotic lawnmowers, powered by AI, are emerging as a solution to reclaim leisure time, similar to how Roomba transformed vacuuming. While the U.S. market is still nascent, companies like Toro, Husqvarna, and Worx are developing more sophisticated models, moving beyond boundary wires towards GPS and 3D vision technologies. These quiet, autonomous mowers promise neatly cut lawns daily and can integrate with smart home ecosystems, freeing homeowners from the chore of mowing.

title: Morgan Health makes $30M investment in Centivo
summary: Morgan Health, JPMorgan Chase's healthcare arm, has invested $30 million in Centivo, a health plan targeting self-funded employers. Centivo's model focuses on partnering with accountable care organizations to offer affordable, high-quality care, resulting in significant savings for its employer clients. This investment is part of Centivo's extended Series B-1 financing to support its growth and expansion across 13 states.

title: 3 Reasons Why Investing in the Nasdaq-100 Is Effective
summary: This article highlights three core reasons why investing in the Nasdaq-100 is effective for long-term asset management. It explains how index investing, particularly in the Nasdaq-100, offers exposure to rapidly growing, innovative global companies with strong brand power and historically high growth rates. The article details various investment products available, such as mutual funds and ETFs, and discusses strategies like currency hedging and leverage.

title: SnapMirror in the Cloud: New Uses for NetApp Data Replication
summary: NetApp's SnapMirror, a long-standing enterprise data replication solution, is now extended to the cloud through Cloud Volumes ONTAP. This integration opens up new use cases for SnapMirror, including cloud-based disaster recovery, efficient cloud migration, application development and analytics, and multicloud architecture. It also plays a role in NetApp Cloud Backup, enhancing data protection and efficiency across hybrid and multicloud environments by leveraging block-level replication and storage efficiencies like deduplication and compression.

title: If AI had a voice!
summary: This article explores the inherent gender bias in Artificial Intelligence, arguing that AI often reflects and amplifies the biases of its creators. Through examples like language translation and common AI voice assistants, the author demonstrates how AI frequently defaults to male coding for leadership roles and female for assistive roles, mirroring societal stereotypes. While acknowledging that machine learning is evolving to address these biases, the piece emphasizes the ongoing need for greater inclusion and feedback to achieve true gender neutrality in AI development.

title: Keystone RV will close two Goshen plants, putting 334 out of work. Here's what we know.
summary: Keystone RV has announced the closure of two plants in Goshen, Indiana, effective September 23, 2022, resulting in 334 job losses. The company, a subsidiary of Thor Industries, cited a need to level off production after record-setting years, despite overall RV shipments remaining strong. While retail sales have slowed, local officials note a continued demand for labor in Elkhart County.

title: SkyWater unveils plans to build $1.8 bln chip facility in Indiana
summary: U.S. semiconductor manufacturer SkyWater Technology Inc announced plans to invest $1.8 billion in a chip research and production facility in Indiana, in partnership with the state and Purdue University. The project is contingent on the passage of the CHIPS Act, which aims to provide billions in subsidies and tax credits to the semiconductor industry. This move is seen as crucial for reshoring semiconductor manufacturing and will benefit from collaboration with Purdue University's talent pipeline.

title: Yelp's departure is a blow for city's office market
summary: Yelp's decision to close its New York City offices and embrace a fully remote workforce is a significant blow to the city's office market, particularly for landlords in downtown Manhattan. The departure of Yelp from its 200,000 square feet at 11 Madison Square, along with other tech company retrenchments, highlights a trend of vacated spaces not being refilled, impacting the commercial real estate sector. This move reflects a broader shift by tech firms towards remote work models, leaving landlords concerned about the future of office occupancy.

title: Local Bounti Debuts New Production Facility in Georgia
summary: Local Bounti, an indoor leafy greens grower, announced the commencement of farming operations at its new controlled-environment agriculture facility in Byron, GA. This new facility establishes a bi-coastal presence for the company, expanding its distribution capabilities to 19 retail distribution centers within a 400-mile radius and servicing approximately 10,000 retail locations. Local Bounti also plans to expand the facility's capacity and introduce its Stack & Flow Technology to meet growing demand and broaden its product offerings.

title: Morgan Stanley, NEF Commit $250M for Affordable Housing
summary: Morgan Stanley and National Equity Fund have committed $250 million in funding to BRIDGE Housing Corp. for affordable and workforce housing initiatives. This investment will benefit low- and middle-income residents nationally and is expected to leverage up to an additional $1 billion in capital. The funds will be used for property acquisitions, land purchases, refinancing, capital improvements, and acquiring general partner interests.

title: Amazon and One Medical agree to acquisition of One Medical
summary: Amazon has entered into a definitive merger agreement to acquire One Medical, a human-centered, technology-powered U.S. primary care organization, for $18 per share in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $3.9 billion. This acquisition aims to reinvent the healthcare experience by making quality care more affordable, accessible, and enjoyable through a seamless combination of in-person, digital, and virtual care services. Amir Dan Rubin will remain CEO of One Medical after the completion of the transaction, which is subject to customary closing conditions, including shareholder and regulatory approval.

title: The World’s Largest Asset Manager BlackRock Lost $2.46 Trillion In The First Half Of 2022
summary: BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager, lost US$1.7 trillion (AU$2.46 trillion) in the first half of 2022 due to tumultuous financial markets, high inflation, and rising interest rates. Assets under management fell 11% to US$8.49 trillion, and adjusted profit decreased significantly compared to 2021. Despite these losses and retail investor withdrawals, the firm still attracted US$89.6 billion in new investments.

title: Comparing Kroger’s and Albertsons’ delivery membership programs
summary: Kroger has expanded its Boost delivery membership program nationwide, offering free delivery at two annual subscription levels and perks like bonus fuel savings. Albertsons also offers a similar program, FreshPass, which provides free delivery and other rewards such as a monthly Starbucks credit. Both grocers are using these subscription models, added to existing loyalty programs, to enhance customer loyalty and grow their e-commerce operations, competing with major players like Amazon and Walmart.

title: 7 Reasons Why People Are Moving to Texas
summary: Texas has become a popular relocation destination, drawing nearly 4 million new residents between 2010 and 2020. This article explores the key factors attracting people to the Lone Star State, including a lower cost of living, more affordable housing, no state income tax, and a thriving job market. Additionally, Texas boasts great schools, a warm climate, and rich cultural diversity, making it an appealing option for many.

title: Amazon is buying One Medical for $3.49 billion in latest move to dominate healthcare industry
summary: Amazon announced its acquisition of primary-care company One Medical for $3.49 billion, marking its latest significant move into the healthcare market. One Medical operates 182 medical offices across 25 U.S. markets, offering subscribers access to physicians and digital health services. This acquisition follows Amazon's previous ventures into healthcare, including an online pharmacy and a primary-care clinic for employees, signaling a continued effort to reinvent healthcare experiences.

title: Amazon to Buy One Medical for $3.49 Billion in All-Cash Deal
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has announced its intention to acquire the primary-care company One Medical for $18 per share, an all-cash deal valued at $3.49 billion. This acquisition marks Amazon's continued expansion into the healthcare sector, making it one of the company's largest deals to date. One Medical operates medical clinics across various markets in the United States.

title: Amazon (AMAZ) to Use Rivian Vans as EV Maker Works Toward Delivery Goal
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is beginning to deliver packages to U.S. customers using electric vans manufactured by Rivian Automotive Inc. The retail giant expects to deploy thousands of these vans this year, out of a total order of up to 100,000 vehicles. This rollout marks a significant step for Rivian as it works to meet its delivery goals.

title: GM’s OnStar Unveils New Brand Identity, Expands Services as Company Ushers in New Era of Safety
summary: OnStar has announced a new brand identity and expanded its safety and security services, introducing OnStar Guardian for motorcycle riders and integrating with Amazon Alexa for in-home emergency assistance. These developments reflect OnStar's commitment to making safety accessible to more people, both in and outside of vehicles, and GM's push into software innovation and subscription services. The OnStar Guardian app is now available to anyone with a compatible smartphone, even those without a GM vehicle.

title: Johnson & Johnson leans on beauty trends to create Vivvi & Bloom baby care brand
summary: Johnson & Johnson launched a new baby care brand, Vivvi & Bloom, inspired by beauty industry trends and designed to appeal to millennial and Gen-Z parents with natural formulas and a community-led development approach. This premium brand aims to capture a larger share of the baby care market, despite a recent decline in J&J's consumer health sales attributed to supply chain constraints. Vivvi & Bloom's strategy involves co-creation with parents and a digital-first marketing approach to differentiate itself from existing J&J baby lines like Johnson's Baby and Aveeno Baby.

title: Walmart partnership expands The Honest Company’s reach
summary: The Honest Company is expanding its distribution network by partnering with Walmart, making its products available on Walmart's website and in physical stores this fall. This move aims to increase accessibility for customers and generate capital to support the company's growth, which has historically relied significantly on retail partnerships, including Target, Amazon, and Costco. The expansion is part of Honest Company's omni-channel retail strategy and Walmart's effort to offer trustworthy products.

title: NVDS Share Price & Live Chart | AXS 1.25X NVDA Bear Daily ETF
summary: This article provides live share price data, historical performance charts, and technical analysis for the AXS 1.25X NVDA Bear Daily ETF (NVDS). It details key metrics such as dividend yield, expense ratio, holdings, and long-term performance trends. Investors can access current share price, market data, and evaluate the ETF's suitability for their portfolio through InvestingPro's WarrenAI.

title: Receiving money via apps? Selling items online? It may affect your taxes
summary: New tax laws, specifically the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA), have changed the reporting requirements for online sales. For the 2025 calendar year (2026 filing season), a 1099-K form will be issued if transactions exceed $20,000 and there are over 200 transactions. This article from H&R Block explains how to report online sales, whether for personal items, hobbies, or businesses, and provides guidance on tax forms like 1099-K, Schedule D, and Form 8949.

title: Tuya Announces Matter-compatible Solutions in Close Collaboration with Amazon Alexa
summary: Tuya Smart announced its collaboration with Amazon Alexa to implement Frustration-Free Setup (FFS) based on the Matter connectivity protocol, aiming to enhance the IoT device setup experience and allow direct Wi-Fi connections to Amazon Echo devices. Tuya, an initial FFS partner for Matter, is participating in interoperability tests with Amazon, Google, and Apple and plans to launch Matter-compatible devices by the end of 2022. The company is committed to promoting universal open standards in IoT and supporting its ecosystem partners in adopting Matter, enabling a wider variety of smart home solutions for consumers.

title: Target to Open Hubs in Chicago, Denver
summary: Target Corp. announced plans to open three new package-sorting centers, two in greater Chicago and one in the Denver area, to enhance its strategy of using stores to fulfill online orders. This expansion will bring their total mini-warehouses to nine across the U.S., with more planned, aiming to accelerate local deliveries and reduce shipping costs by fulfilling orders from stores. The retailer is leveraging its acquisitions of Shipt, Grand Junction, and Deliv to optimize last-mile delivery, increase efficiency, and lower costs amid surging digital sales.

title: News | Amazon Buys Up Thousands of Acres As It Eyes Future Real Estate Needs
summary: Amazon is shifting its real estate strategy from leasing to owning, having spent billions on acquiring over 5,000 acres since early 2020 for logistics centers. This move comes as the e-commerce giant slows its warehouse leasing and plans to sublet millions of square feet amid economic shifts. Despite fears of a pullback, this strategic change could offer opportunities for other businesses to occupy Amazon's vacated or subleased spaces in a tight industrial market.

title: Tracking the development of Kroger’s automated e-commerce center network
summary: Kroger's ambitious plan, announced in 2018, to create a nationwide network of robotic e-commerce fulfillment centers with Ocado began with energetic openings in 2021 and continued through late 2023. However, the project has faced mounting challenges, including the closure of multiple "spokes" and customer fulfillment centers (CFCs) since May 2024, and a recent cancellation of a planned North Carolina CFC. This article provides a continually updated tracker of Kroger's automated e-commerce network, detailing facility openings and closures as the grocer refines its online fulfillment strategy.

title: Top stock reports to watch this week (25.07.2022)
summary: The article highlights the key earnings reports scheduled for the week of July 25, 2022, focusing on major US tech companies like Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta Platforms, Amazon, and Apple. It notes that the Wall Street earnings season is in full swing, with several Dow Jones members also reporting their financial results. This week is expected to be significant for traders due to the high-profile companies announcing their earnings.

title: Healthcare Triangle launches regional HQ in Singapore to bolster medical innovation in APAC
summary: Healthcare Triangle Inc. has inaugurated its regional headquarters in Singapore, planning to invest $25 million to advance digital healthcare across the Asia Pacific region. This expansion aims to foster medical innovation, create over 500 jobs, and support the digital transformation of healthcare and pharmaceutical sectors by leveraging cloud-based platforms. The company's focus includes strategic partnerships and collaborations to build a more resilient healthcare ecosystem in the APAC region.

title: Mitsubishi Materials Corporation Selects SAP’s Cloud Offering, RISE with SAP
summary: Mitsubishi Materials Corporation has chosen SAP's cloud solutions, including RISE with SAP and SAP S/4HANA Cloud, to modernize its core accounting and enterprise information systems. This move is part of the company's broader digital transformation strategy to enhance business value, operational competitiveness, and management efficiency. The implementation will leverage Amazon Web Services and integrate other SAP platforms like SAP Business Technology Platform and SAP Signavio.

title: Sun Country CEO: Europe, wide-body aircraft, small cities in airline's future
summary: Sun Country Airlines CEO Jude Bricker discusses the airline's future plans, which include expanding into Europe, utilizing wide-body aircraft for both cargo and passenger services, and serving smaller cities. These initiatives are part of the budget carrier's strategy to capitalize on government-subsidized routes.

title: Amazon to raise Prime prices in Europe as retailer wrestles with costs
summary: Amazon announced it will increase prices for its Prime delivery and streaming service in Europe by up to 43% annually, effective September 15. This move follows a similar hike in the U.S. and is attributed to rising inflation, increased operating costs, and investments in faster delivery and more content. The decision comes as Amazon faces pressure to improve profitability amidst a challenging economic environment, having reported its first quarterly loss in seven years in April.

title: Manufacturing Titan 3M Is Spinning Off Its Healthcare Business Into A Separate Company
summary: 3M announced its plan to spin off its healthcare division into a separate, publicly traded company. This new healthcare entity, with approximately $8.6 billion in sales in 2021, will focus on innovation in areas like wound care, oral care, healthcare IT, and biopharma filtration. The move aims to create two well-capitalized companies better positioned to pursue their respective growth strategies.

title: Rumors of Oracle Layoffs Highlight Company's Position in Cloud Race
summary: Rumors are circulating about potential Oracle layoffs affecting thousands of workers across multiple divisions, following reports from The Information and CRN. This comes as Oracle intensifies its efforts to compete in the cloud market against giants like AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud, despite facing an uphill battle in developer preference. While Oracle has secured wins like TikTok as a cloud client and offers competitive salaries for in-demand tech roles, its broad transformation to keep pace in the rapidly evolving cloud landscape is under scrutiny amid tech industry hiring slowdowns.

title: Walmart profit woes hit retail stocks, deepen consumer spending concerns
summary: Walmart's reduced profit forecast has caused a significant drop in retail stocks, including Amazon and Target, highlighting concerns about consumer spending slowing due to high inflation. Analysts view Walmart's announcement as a serious indicator of the average American household's financial strain, particularly in discretionary categories like apparel. The situation puts pressure on the Federal Reserve as it considers interest rate hikes to combat inflation while trying to avoid a recession.

title: Corsair K70 Pro Mini wireless review: "one hell of a feature list"
summary: The Corsair K70 Pro Mini is the brand's first hot-swappable 60% gaming keyboard, offering numerous features like 50 onboard profiles, Bluetooth and 2.4GHz wireless connectivity, and an 8,000Hz polling rate when wired. While praised for its design and gaming performance, the typing experience can be "scratchy" due to the stock Cherry MX switches and stabilizer rattle, making it less ideal for productivity. Despite its higher price, it's considered a strong contender for gamers seeking a miniature powerhouse, though alternatives exist for those prioritizing typing feel or a lower cost.

title: RYU’s Wholesale Strategy an Unprecedented Success with Addition of Former Saks Fifth Ave SVP, National Expansion, and New Partnerships with Wholesale Icons such as Zappos, Urban Outfitters, Nordstroms, and Others
summary: RYU Apparel Inc. is experiencing dramatic growth in its Q2 2022 wholesale strategy, exceeding expectations due to the addition of Thomas Ott, former Saks Fifth Avenue SVP, to lead its wholesale push. The company announced new partnerships with major retailers like Nordstroms, Urban Outfitters, and Zappos, complementing existing relationships with Altitude Sports and Winners. RYU plans to expand its wholesale channels through traditional stockholding retailers, drop-shipping partnerships, and premium clearance accounts, with strategic goals for its Impact and Rebel collections through 2024.

title: Amazon's new KC-area lease is in the same location, but with a smaller size
summary: Amazon has signed a new lease for a warehouse in the Kansas City area, returning to a site where it previously canceled plans for a larger project. The move comes as Amazon evaluates its nationwide warehouse needs due to slowing e-commerce demand. The new facility will be smaller than the previously planned project, but is located in the same industrial park.

title: Dick’s Sporting Goods debuts virtual high school experience on Roblox
summary: Dick's Sporting Goods has launched a virtual "School of Sport" experience on Roblox to engage younger shoppers during the back-to-school season. Users can customize avatars, participate in challenges, and earn style points, aiming to connect with Gen Z in the metaverse. This initiative aligns with a new "Sport Your Style" campaign and taps into Roblox's popularity among retailers targeting younger demographics.

title: FedEx Ground affirms ban on 3rd-party negotiations with contractors
summary: FedEx Ground has reaffirmed its policy against negotiating with third parties representing groups of contractors, insisting on individual agreements. This comes in response to a contractor, Spencer Patton, attempting to organize other contractors to collectively negotiate financial terms, citing rising costs. FedEx Ground CEO John Smith stated that such group negotiations breach existing contracts and emphasized that service reliability has improved, contrary to Patton's claims about turbulence impacting deliveries.

title: How Zoom security incident response survived the pandemic
summary: During the COVID-19 pandemic, Zoom experienced an exponential increase in users, forcing a massive, rapid scaling of its incident response operation and observability infrastructure. The company addressed security concerns by significantly expanding its security data log infrastructure and implementing new security protocols, executive hires, and a freeze on non-security related features. Leveraging AWS services like Kinesis, Lambda, and S3, Zoom built a scalable, event-driven architecture to manage petabytes of data, and further enhanced its security posture with Splunk's SOAR tool to automate incident triage and improve alert efficiency.

title: Congressional probe labels Siegel Group’s eviction practices ‘uniquely egregious’
summary: A U.S. House committee investigation found Siegel Suites used abusive tactics, including "deceptive and potentially unlawful practices," to evict tenants during the pandemic, even those approved for rental assistance. The report called The Siegel Group's actions "uniquely egregious" and revealed nearly 15,000 eviction filings by four corporate landlords under investigation. Despite receiving rental assistance and PPP loans, Siegel continued evicting tenants, leading to severe hardship for individuals like Ashima Carter, who struggled with housing and credit damage.

title: KT ups ante with $1.5 billion spending on public sector cloud service
summary: KT Cloud Corp., a subsidiary of South Korea's telecom giant KT Corp., plans to invest up to 2 trillion won ($1.5 billion) over the next three years to expand its presence in the domestic public cloud service sector and enhance its internet data center (IDC) capacity. This move comes as competition intensifies in the Korean cloud market, with local rivals like Naver Cloud and NHN Cloud also aggressively expanding, and foreign players such as Snowflake, Amazon's AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform dominating the broader market. However, local companies are seen to have an advantage in the public sector due to meeting specific government security requirements.

title: EHR on Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
summary: This article discusses how Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP helps healthcare organizations migrate electronic health records (EHRs) to the cloud, addressing challenges like cost reduction, performance, and data management. It emphasizes the partnership between NetApp and AWS in enabling this transition, highlighting benefits such as faster upgrades and improved data protection. The solution aims to free healthcare providers from data center burdens, allowing them to focus on patient outcomes and innovation.

title: P&G Leverages Digital to Drive Sales, Internal Productivity
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) is using digital technologies to enhance both its internal efficiency and its ability to attract consumers amidst challenges like supply chain disruptions and inflation. The company's CEO, Jon Moeller, highlighted the use of AI and blockchain as tools to delight consumers and customers cost-effectively. P&G's CFO, Andre Schulten, noted that over half of their advertising budget is allocated to digital channels, aligning with the growing consumer preference for eCommerce and online grocery shopping.

title: H|T: The Healthtech Times – Amazon is buying into primary care with One Medical acquisition
summary: This article from "H|T: The Healthtech Times" reports on Amazon's acquisition of primary care provider One Medical for $3.9 billion. It also covers significant developments in the healthtech sector, including Oncoustics securing $5.5 million CAD for AI-powered liver disease detection, TA Associates investing over $400 million in Intelerad, and Invitae laying off more than 1,000 employees. The piece highlights a cooling trend in digital health investment after a highly active year.

title: Lessons from Target’s cloud journey, a decade in the making
summary: Target embarked on its cloud journey a decade ago, moving beyond a simple "lift and shift" to a hybrid multicloud architecture supported by Google Cloud Platform and Microsoft Azure. The retailer modernized its application stack with a microservices approach and open-source tools, overcoming initial cost challenges through significant investment in engineering and FinOps. Target plans to continue its hybrid strategy, leveraging public cloud for scalability and cost arbitrage, and private cloud for data-intensive and core business applications.

title: The Weekly Closeout: Lululemon launches its third shoe and Williams Sonoma’s president resigns
summary: This weekly retail roundup highlights Lululemon's launch of its third shoe, the Chargefeel cross-training shoe, and the resignation of Williams Sonoma's president, Ryan Ross, who is replaced by Felix Carbullido. Other news includes Adidas signing 15 female college athletes to NIL deals, Lids opening university-focused retail stores, Best Buy's new small-format store design, and Miller Lite's BodegaWear collection. The article also touches on Shopify's significant net loss and layoffs, and Amazon's planned Prime membership fee increases in Europe due to rising costs.

title: Walmart Hawks Refurbished Goods to Inflation-Squeezed Shoppers
summary: Walmart is launching a "Walmart Restored" program to sell refurbished goods from brands like Apple, Samsung, and KitchenAid, both online and in some stores this fall. This initiative aims to attract cost-conscious shoppers amidst high inflation by offering inspected, tested, and cleaned products with 90-day free returns. The move comes after Walmart cut its profit forecast, noting that rising food and fuel prices are causing customers to reduce spending on general merchandise.

title: PLDT activates trans-Pacific cable system seen to boost Philippine int’l data capacity
summary: PLDT Inc. has activated the Jupiter Cable System, a trans-Pacific cable network that will significantly boost the Philippines' international data capacity. This $136 million investment connects the Philippines to Japan and Los Angeles, tripling PLDT's international capacity to about 60 terabits per second. The system is expected to enhance internet speed and reliability for Filipinos, supporting the nation's digital economy and data-driven industries.

title: How Amazon, Starbucks and other companies fight unions | Robert Reich
summary: Robert Reich details four common union-busting tactics employed by large corporations such as Amazon and Starbucks: anti-union propaganda, hiring expensive anti-union consultants, intentionally delaying unionization votes, and outright breaking labor laws. He highlights that despite these efforts, workers are increasingly unionizing and public opinion supports labor rights. Reich advocates for the PRO Act to strengthen protections for union organizers and level the playing field.
